press_references.value: Repertoire® Immune Medicines Announces Strategic Collaboration with Lilly to Develop Tolerizing Therapies for Autoimmune Diseases

partnership_announcements.description: Repertoire Immune Medicines and Eli Lilly formed a strategic collaboration to discover and develop tolerizing T cell–targeted therapies for multiple autoimmune diseases, with Repertoire leading early discovery and Lilly handling later development and commercialization.

press_references.value: Repertoire® Immune Medicines Enters into Collaboration and License Agreement with Genentech for the Development of T cell-Targeted Therapies for an Autoimmune Disease

partnership_announcements.description: Repertoire Immune Medicines has entered into a collaboration and license agreement with Genentech to discover and develop T cell-targeted therapies for autoimmune diseases. Repertoire will use its DECODE platform for target discovery, while Genentech will handle preclinical, clinical development, and commercialization. The agreement includes $35 million upfront and up to $730 million in milestone payments, plus tiered royalties for Repertoire.

research_insight_text_link.research_insight_description: Repertoire Immune Medicines is engaged in developing immunostimulatory fusion molecules that combine an immune cell targeting moiety with a cytokine molecule. These compositions are designed for pharmaceutical applications and involve specific methods for their use and formulation. Additionally, the company is exploring the use of reversible linkers in protein therapeutics, focusing on their preparation and delivery. These areas of research highlight the company's focus on innovative approaches to immune modulation and therapeutic delivery.

overview_description.description: Repertoire Immune Medicines is a clinical stage biotechnology company working to unleash the human immune system to prevent, treat or cure cancer, autoimmune conditions and infectious diseases. The company is currently conducting experimental medicine clinical trials using autologous T cells primed against cancer antigens and tethered to IL-15.
